headline: World's Largest Battery Ferry Completes Epic Ocean Journey
meta_description: A 130-meter electric ferry built in Tasmania completed a trans-Pacific voyage to Uruguay, marking a milestone in sustainable maritime transport.
summary_short: The world's largest battery-electric ferry has arrived in South America after crossing the Pacific Ocean, heralding a new era for clean shipping.
body:
When Buquebus ordered a diesel ferry in 2019, no one predicted it would become the world's largest electric vehicle ever built. But during the pandemic, as production paused, the South American transport company made an audacious decision: redesign the entire 130-meter ship for battery-electric propulsion instead. The result, Hull 096, left Hobart in early August aboard a heavy-lift transporter, traveled past New Zealand, crossed the Pacific Ocean, rounded Cape Horn, and arrived in Uruguayan waters last Friday. The voyage itself was a feat—one of the most complex marine operations in Tasmanian history—but the destination tells the real story.

This remarkable vessel, to be called China Zorrilla when operational, will spend its working life crossing a single river: the Rio de la Plata between Colonia del Sacramento and Buenos Aires. The 30-nautical-mile route takes roughly an hour. Yet the ship that traveled halfway around the world to reach it carries over 5,000 battery modules and can run for 90 minutes on a full charge—more than sufficient for its modest mission. Built from aluminum to maximize efficiency, it will carry up to 2,100 passengers and 225 vehicles per crossing.

What makes this story truly significant is what it signals beyond one river. Hundreds of Tasmanian shipbuilders contributed to this vessel over several years, and their work has caught international attention. The Danish company Molslinjen has already ordered three similar electric ferries, currently under construction in Hobart, destined for one of northern Europe's busiest corridors. Hull 096 is not the end of a remarkable journey—it marks the beginning of cleaner maritime transport worldwide.
quick_facts: 130-meter battery ferry built in Hobart, Tasmania
Crossed the Pacific Ocean from Australia to Uruguay
Runs on over 5,000 battery modules with 90-minute range
Will serve Rio de la Plata route between Buenos Aires and Colonia del Sacramento
Denmark has ordered three more Incat electric ferries
